conceptual_explanation: The 5** summit of Word Form Accuracy requires distinguishing between near-identical word pairs (Sensible vs Sensitive) and mastering academic nuances (Economic vs Economical). You must also handle rare prefixes and sophisticated suffix shifts that change the intensity or scope of a word's meaning.

rule_cards.name: The 'Sens' Duo
rule_cards.correct: It is a sensible decision to save money. / He is sensitive to cold weather.
rule_cards.incorrect: It is a sensitive decision to save money.

rule_cards.name: Economic vs Economical
rule_cards.formula: Economic (Related to the economy) vs Economical (Saving money/Cheap to run)
rule_cards.correct: The country is facing an economic crisis. / This car is very economical on fuel.
rule_cards.incorrect: The country is facing an economical crisis.

rule_cards.name: Compliment vs Complement
rule_cards.correct: We received complimentary tickets. / Their skills are complementary.
rule_cards.incorrect: Their skills are complimentary. (Unless they praise each other)

rule_cards.name: Noun Nuance: Confidence vs Confidentiality
rule_cards.correct: She spoke with great confidence. / We must respect the confidentiality of the records.
rule_cards.incorrect: We must respect the confidence of the records.

head_noun_tasks.explanation: 'Complementary' (with an 'e') means it completes or works well with the existing systems.
'Economic' refers to the general state of the economy.
'Sensitive' here refers to being easily affected emotionally.
'Confidentiality' refers to the state of keeping information private.

drill_tasks.question: It would be ________ to bring an umbrella, as the forecast predicts rain.
The government is implementing new ________ policies to curb inflation.
drill_tasks.explanation: Refers to policies related to the national economy.

drill_tasks.question: The two colors ________ each other perfectly in this design.
drill_tasks.explanation: Verb meaning to match or complete (with 'e').

drill_tasks.question: He has a lot of ________ in his ability to lead the team.
This energy-saving light bulb is very ________.
drill_tasks.explanation: Means avoiding waste or being cheap to run.

boss_fight.paragraph: It was a sensitive decision to invest in this economical project during the current financial crisis. The manager gave us complement tickets to the theater to boost our confidentiality in the company.

errors.explanation: Refers to a project related to the economy, or perhaps just a 'sensible' one, but 'economic' fits the crisis context.

success_feedback: Incredible! You have mastered the most treacherous word form pairs in the English language. Your 5** precision is outstanding.
suggested_next_steps: Read legal or economic reports to see these nuances in practice.
Study how prefixes like 'Counter-' and 'Anti-' are used in academic debates.
Create your own 'Confusing Pairs' list to test your friends!
